key_insight: SCODEL improves food entity linking by giving contextual recipe mentions and matching ontology concepts shared canonical definitions.
clinical_relevance: The approach may support biomedical terminology linking, but this study does not establish clinical utility or patient benefit.
method: Use shared ontology-oriented definitions as a semantic normalisation layer.
Augment ReFinED, GSM-EL and BLINK without introducing a new linking architecture.
Link recipe food mentions to build an ontology-grounded knowledge graph.
evidence_signal: On the new ReciLinkD benchmark, SCODEL × BLINK reached 88.33% Hit@1 for seen concepts and SCODEL × GSM-EL reached 83.15% for unseen concepts; a biomedical ontology benchmark also showed generalisation.
watch_item: Clinical deployment would require task-specific validation; the abstract does not report biomedical benchmark details or clinical outcomes.
paper_title: SCODEL: Shared Canonical Ontology Definitions for Food Entity Linking and Ontology-Grounded Recipe Knowledge Graphs
